newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas holds on storage, cooling demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas holds on storage, cooling demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were little changed Wednesday as short-term buying continued in the warmer-than-normal Northeast and buyers packed more gas into storage, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices at the Henry Hub rose to a high of $2.18 early as NYMEX's July gas futures opened to a high of $2.155, up 3.3 cents from Tuesday.
As futures began to falter, Henry Hub prices slipped to about $2.14-2.15 shortly before nomination deadlines, traders said.
In the Northeast, where some temperature highs were breaking through 90 degrees F, New York city gate prices were well supported in the low-$2.40s, market sources said.
According to WSC, temperatures in the Northeast are expected to return to near normal by the weekend and then slightly below normal early next week.

In south Texas, prices were little changed at $2.08-2.10, traders said. Temperatures in Houston were expected to reach highs of 91 and 92 degrees F on Thursday and Friday, respectively, according to Weather Services Corp (WSC).
In west Texas, Permian prices gained about two cents to $1.95-1.98, while Waha values were quoted at $2.04-2.05.
Southern California prices also remained firm at $2.13-2.17 despite temperature high readings only in the mid-to-high 70s F in Los Angeles.

Providing additional energy to the market was the full return of the 1,221 megawatt Palo Verde 2 nuclear unit, near Phoenix, Ariz., as reported by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission in its plant status report.

Cooler weather is moving toward the Southwest and is expected to push temperatures to about four to eight degrees F below normal this weekend, WSC reported, adding that warmer weather is forecast to return early next week.
In the Midwest, prices held at $2.00-2.04, with the lower-priced deals reported done in late trading.
Temperatures in the region are forecast to drop to normal to slightly below-normal levels through the weekend before returning to a few degrees above normal early next week, WSC reported.
Separately, injection estimates for today's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 80 to 110 bcf, with most estimates at 90-100 bcf. Stocks rose 88 bcf a year ago.
